results.Notes: PASS. Full canonical-bank review found related administration items, but this item uniquely tests routine MH/SUD administration workflow: patient-specific single-dose handling, administration-record documentation, encouraged prescriber transmission, and privacy. Q0175 instead tests serious adverse-event follow-through; Q0145 tests category authorization. The SATA distractors target delegation and privacy errors rather than mere schedule recall.

PASS. Full-bank comparison shows a distinct applied corresponding-responsibility problem. Q0193 tests the general methadone indication/pathway matrix and Q0194 directly tests an explicitly OUD-maintenance retail prescription; Q0164 instead presents contradictory pain labeling and patient-reported OTP replacement, requiring clarification before pathway selection. Q0162/Q0163 are generic corresponding-responsibility items without the methadone indication conflict.

PASS. This is the baseline rule-architecture SATA for the narrow non-OTP emergency pathway: dispense rather than prescribe, three days at one time, referral bridge, and no renewal/extension. Q0195 is meaningfully different because it applies those limits to a planned recurring weekly methadone scheme. The item requires combining multiple regulatory conditions rather than recalling a drug schedule.

Q0171 tests which drug/indication categories fall within pharmacist administration authority; Q0172 assumes listed MH/SUD medications and tests the second-stage eligibility gates of adult age, no pharmacist-administered first dose, patient-specific prescription, and single-dose presentation. The scenarios are practice-plausible and require option-by-option application.

Q0146 tests absence of patient-specific prescription/prescriber authorization, while Q0173 intentionally supplies those prerequisites and isolates a different administrator-qualification defect: expired CPR certification. The waiver-style distractors are realistic scope/compliance traps and the Vivitrol context is necessary rather than decorative.

Q0147 covers routine MH/SUD administration workflow; Q0175 adds a severe post-administration reaction requiring emergency care and tests the distinct immediate prescriber-reporting trigger, pharmacy administration-record duty, and preserved Board-reporting responsibility. Q0056/Q0115 concern serious events arising from dispensing errors, not this administration-guidance follow-through pathway.

PASS. The item integrates methadone schedule identity with indication-dependent pain versus OUD pathways and the narrow non-OTP emergency bridge. Q0194 is a single explicit OUD-maintenance retail scenario and Q0164 adds a contradictory-indication corresponding-responsibility conflict, so this matrix remains a distinct synthesis item rather than a duplicate or schedule flashcard.

PASS. Although several distractors are intentionally clear at difficulty 3, the central A-versus-B choice tests the common legal error of treating methadone identically regardless of indication. It is distinct from Q0193's broader matrix and Q0164's ambiguity/clarification scenario. The item is concise, practice-based, and does not rely on schedule memorization alone.

PASS. Q0165 asks for the baseline elements of 21 CFR 1306.07(b); Q0195 instead tests whether a practitioner may serially reuse the exception as planned weekly maintenance without referral. The recurring-supply scenario forces the learner to read the three-day quantity limit together with referral and no-renewal/no-extension language, making it a distinct applied jurisprudence item.
